messages:
li: Quick brain-dump — we should move from a single fixed tokens/min quota to an adaptive windowed quota + soft-isolation for noisy tenants. Current problem: big short bursts evict KV cache and spike tail latency for other tenants.

maya: Agree. What's your idea for windows?

li: Two-level counters: micro_window (30s) for burst control + macro_window (1h) for long-term fairness. Micro window uses a dampening factor so repeated bursts decay faster. If micro_window breached -> apply short diversion to cheaper quantized model or soft-throttle.

andrew: How would abuse scoring integrate? Do we block onscore checks?

li: Score stays async. We increment a lightweight heuristic counter on suspect patterns (high tokens/sec, many unique prompt signatures). If heuristics exceed threshold, mark tenant as "probation" and tighten micro_window. ML-based score updates offline and influence macro_window weights.

sam: Implementation ops note: storing micro counters per-tenant in Redis will cause hotkey pressure. Suggest local in-process token buckets for immediate checks and a sampled async write-back to Redis. 

li: Exactly. Enforcement flow I imagine: request -> local bucket check (best-effort) -> fallback to regional redis global counter -> if fail route to fallback model or 429. Also emit metric + billing event for fallback.

maya: We need a clear fallback policy matrix (when to 429 vs fallback to cheaper model vs queue). Also ensure headers for clients: e.g. X-Quota-Policy, X-Quota-Remaining.

li: Example header plan: 
```
X-Quota-Policy: window=30s;micro_used=720;micro_limit=1000;status=soft-isolated
X-Quota-Next-Action: fallback=quantized-v2;fallback-reason=burst
```

andrew: Perf implementation detail: for sliding window use fixed-size ring counters per-shard (N buckets in a minute window) to avoid per-request atomic ops. We can approximate counts cheaply and correct with periodic aggregates.

sam: Also need abuse signal hygiene to avoid false positives (e.g., short-lived legitimate spikes like training bursts). Make probation time window exponential backoff rather than fixed kickouts.

li: Good point. Probation time = min(1h * 2^n, 24h) where n increments per incident. Reset on several clean windows.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary plan created: eng-infra region-a -> quota-algo-v2 -> 10% traffic -> monitoring alerts for p50/p95/p99 and error-rate. Canary start 2026-05-03T03:00:00Z.

maya: Action items: 1) PoC local token-bucket + ring-counter (owner: sam) 2) Abuse scoring RFC + offline model contract (owner: andrew) 3) Fallback policy matrix + client header spec (owner: maya) 4) Canary dashboard + alerts (owner: li). PRs targeted EOD next Tue.

andrew: I'll draft the scoring contract and include evaluation metrics (false-positive rate <= 1%, recall on automated abuse >= 80%).

li: I'll start the RFC skeleton. Keep this thread for quick syncs. TL;DR: micro+macro windows, local fast path, async abuse scoring, quantized-model fallback, exponential probation.

sam: ack, starting PoC tomorrow.

maya: Thanks — let's avoid global 429s where possible; fallback safer and better customer experience. :+1:

li: +1, will include rollout/kill-switch notes in RFC.
